title: Ac voltage generation
summary: Explains how an alternator generates ac emf, the frequency formula f = N × P, and how to calculate instantaneous emf e = E sinΦ for angles up to 360°.

sections.heading: Generating emf
paragraphs: As the coil in a simple alternator rotates through 360°, the output voltage rises from 0 V to the peak value, falls to 0 V, and repeats in the opposite polarity. The polarity of the induced emf is found with Fleming's right hand rule.

Thumb: direction of motion. First finger: polarity of the field. Second finger: polarity of the conventional current. With the field running north to south and the conductor moving upwards, the current flows towards us.
bullets: Thumb = motion, first finger = field, second finger = conventional current

sections.heading: Frequency of a single-loop ac generator
paragraphs: The frequency of the generated signal depends on the pole pairs and the speed of rotation. One N and S pole make one pair, and the speed N is given in revs/second.
bullets: f = frequency; P = pole pairs; N = speed of rotation (revs/second)

sections.heading: Instantaneous emf
paragraphs: The emf induced in a single loop, single phase ac generator is found from e = E sinΦ, where Φ is the angle at which we wish to find the induced emf and E is the peak value of the induced emf.
bullets: Φ = angle; E = peak value of the induced emf

sections.heading: Angles greater than 90°
paragraphs: For angles of rotation greater than 90°, the angle at the point of measurement is taken as the angle that gives the same emf as an angle between 0° and 90°. For example, when Φ = 60° the emf is 50V; for Φ = 120° subtract from 180 to get 60°, giving the same 50V.

quiz.q: Which formula gives the frequency of a single-loop ac generator?
quiz.why: Frequency f = N × P, with N in revs/second and P as pole pairs.

quiz.q: A generator has 2 pole pairs and turns at 25 revs/second. What is the frequency (f = N × P)?
Which equation gives the emf at angle Φ for a single loop?
quiz.why: The induced emf is e = E sinΦ.

quiz.q: For Φ = 120°, which angle gives the same emf?
quiz.why: For 90° to 180° use sin(180 – Φ) = sin 60°.

quiz.q: Which rule applies for angles between 180° and 270°?
quiz.why: For 180° to 270° the rule is sinΦ = -sin(Φ – 180).

quiz.q: Which rule applies for angles between 270° and 360°?
quiz.why: For 270° to 360° the rule is sinΦ = -sin(360 – Φ).

quiz.q: In Fleming's right hand rule, which finger shows the field polarity?
quiz.why: First finger = polarity of the field.

quiz.q: In e = E sinΦ, what does Φ represent?
options: The angle at which the emf is found
quiz.why: Φ is the angle at which we wish to find the induced emf.

quiz.q: What are the units of speed N in the frequency formula?
quiz.why: N would be given in revs/second.
